questions: Does 'somehow equals' mean exact integer equality, or could it be interpreted as approximate equality within a tolerance?
Are we allowed to use the same element more than once in the permutation (i.e., is B a true permutation of A, or can we reuse numbers)?
Should the output be case-sensitive ('Yes'/'No' exactly as specified) or is any capitalization acceptable?
Is the multiplication standard integer multiplication, or could it be something else like modulo arithmetic or floating-point?
If the product B_1 * B_2 exceeds typical integer limits (e.g., beyond 32-bit), should we handle overflow, or assume it's within bounds?
Can B_1 and B_2 be the same element from A (i.e., can the permutation assign the same original value to both positions if it appears only once)?
Should we consider all permutations of the three elements, or only those where B_1 and B_2 are the first two elements of the permuted sequence?
If A contains duplicate values, are permutations considered distinct based on positions or just on multiset arrangements?
